units.source_text: 在重视胜负的世界里，不切实际地把英雄吹捧上天，也许是观众的一种嗜好。

en.t: In a world that prizes victory and defeat, perhaps it is one of the spectators' tastes to unrealistically exalt a hero to the skies.

units.source_text: 旗鼓相当的对立也可以招人青睐，倒不一定希望优势绝对集中在一人身上。

en.t: A well-matched rivalry can also win people's favor; they do not necessarily want superiority to be concentrated absolutely in one person.

units.source_text: “常胜名人”的高大形象屹立在棋手面前。

en.t: The towering image of the ever-victorious Meijin stood before the players.

units.source_text: 名人也曾有过几次鏖战，把一生的命运都押在上面了。

en.t: The Meijin too had fought several fierce battles, staking the fate of his whole life on them.

units.source_text: 他不曾在最高的弈战中失败过。

en.t: He had never been defeated in the highest contests of play.

units.source_text: 成为名人之前，战斗是振奋人心的；

en.t: Before he became Meijin, his battles were stirring and inspiring;

units.source_text: 成为名人之后，尤其是晚年的战斗，人们都相信他是不败的；

en.t: after he became Meijin, especially in the battles of his later years, people all believed he was invincible;

units.source_text: 面临战斗，他本人也坚信必胜。

en.t: and when facing a battle, he himself firmly believed he was certain to win.
That, in fact, was the tragedy.

units.source_text: 将棋名人关根纵然败北，也毫不在乎，而秀哉名人却吃不消。

en.t: Even if Sekine, the shogi Meijin, lost, he would not mind at all, but Meijin Shusai could not bear it.

units.source_text: 常言道，围棋赛七成是先手取胜，名人执白棋，败给七段也是正常。

en.t: As the saying goes, in go matches the first player wins seventy percent of the time, so with the Meijin taking white, losing to a seventh-dan player was also normal.
Amateurs do not understand this point.
